osaka_oishii_sake_nakayoshi_nipponbashi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the menu includes tempura, a beef cutlet and dishes with ponzu.
osaka_oishii_sake_nakayoshi_nipponbashi.vegan_detail: Ask. Homemade tofu and vegetable tempura are on the menu, but stocks and batters are not described.
osaka_oishii_sake_nakayoshi_nipponbashi.hours_raw: Tue–Sun and holidays 17:00–23:30 (food last order 23:00); closed Monday (Tabelog). Seated without a reservation just before 21:00 on a Friday (August 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Run by two people, so dishes can take a while (February–March 2026).
osaka_oishii_sake_nakayoshi_nipponbashi.notes: [Izakaya · a quiet sake-and-fish izakaya by Kintetsu Nippombashi] A calm 17-seat izakaya a minute from Kintetsu Nippombashi, run by two people, with fish the owner buys at the market and a deep drink list: over 40 sakes kept in a dedicated fridge, 80-plus shochu and 15-plus umeshu. Start with the sashimi platter, then the rolled omelet, brought out on a hot teppan with extra dashi poured on so it bubbles at the table. Diners also praise the fried hatahata, homemade zaru tofu, whitebait with grated daikon and ponzu, mackerel pressed sushi and monkfish liver with nara-zuke. Dishes can take a while, and one diner found many sakes out of stock. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Sake-and-fish izakaya run by two people (March 2026 review; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: The owner buys seasonal fish at the market (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Sashimi platter; dashi rolled omelet; sake.

anecdotes.text: "It's served on a hot teppan, and just before serving, [extra dashi is poured] over it! The steam rises, and the dashi bubbles on the teppan…" — September 2026, Dashimaki.

"…every dish was delicious! I especially enjoyed the pressed sushi with mackerel and the tempura with aonori (seaweed) and onion. It's impressive that [it is managed] with just two people!" — March 2026.

osaka_keshiki_yakitori_higashishinsaibas.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; skewers come with house seasonings such as white wine sauce, escargot butter and black truffle oil (Tabelog listing), and tare is not described.
osaka_keshiki_yakitori_higashishinsaibas.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken specialist; vegetable skewers exist but bastes are not described.
osaka_keshiki_yakitori_higashishinsaibas.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Fri–Sun 18:00–05:00 (last order 04:00); closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog). Phone reservations from Japanese mobile numbers only (Tabelog). Some items depend on supply (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Busy around 19:00, so book (October 2025). Opened 14 September 2019 (Tabelog).
osaka_keshiki_yakitori_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Yakitori · a 10-seat charcoal yakitori counter open to 5 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small counter yakitori bar near Shinsaibashi Station, open from 18:00 until 5 am, so it works for dinner or a 1 am second stop. More than 30 skewer cuts, many rare, come from Tanba chicken, Tokushima young chicken and Daisen Jidori, each grilled over charcoal, and some get unusual house finishes such as escargot butter or black truffle oil. The omakase is good value; add vegetable skewers, the garlic edamame and a comforting egg soup with thin noodles to finish. One diner found the duck tataki weaker than the rest. Reservations by Japanese mobile number only. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Yakitori counter with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh chicken from Tanba, Tokushima and Daisen (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Yakitori with rare cuts and house seasonings.

anecdotes.text: "…you can enjoy a variety of dishes with the omakase option at a low price… The garlic-edamame was a hidden gem! To finish off, I had a comforting egg soup with nyumen noodles." — October 2025.
"I visited around 1:00 AM as my second stop, and the yakitori was fantastic… The duck tataki was a bit disappointing, but everything else was excellent." — October 2025.

osaka_fukutaro_namba_dining_maison.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Fukutaro's department-store counter, Takashimaya 8F, Namba] The Takashimaya branch of Fukutaro, an okonomiyaki house whose main shop is nearby, on the eighth-floor restaurant level: a 15-seat counter where the cooks make each okonomiyaki on the teppan in front of you. The batter is fluffy enough to melt, the sauce measured; get the negiyaki with seasoned beef tendon, a mixed okonomiyaki or a buta-tama with a runny egg, and maybe squid yakisoba. Diners use it to dodge the queue at the main shop, though there's often a short line here too (orders are taken while you wait), and it takes time to cook. Takeout is popular. Weekdays it breaks between 14:30 and 17:00.

chef_bio.origin: Branch of Fukutaro, whose main shop is nearby (September–October 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the squid yakisoba, mixed grill, and negiyaki with tendon. The mixed grill was incredibly tender, and the seasoning on the tendon in the negiyaki was outstanding." — September 2026.
"The perfect grilling on the surface, the juicy and tender batter, generous pieces of pork, and a runny egg combined with a deeply flavorful sauce made it irresistible." — October 2026, Buta-tama.

osaka_sumibi_kushiyaki_hinataya.hours_raw: Daily 16:00–24:00 (last order 23:30); irregular closures; may change, so check (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and PayPay accepted (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Draft beer ¥500 including tax (May 2026). Opened 18 January 2021 (Tabelog).
osaka_sumibi_kushiyaki_hinataya.notes: [Yakitori · a charcoal skewer bar for chicken and pork, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A casual charcoal skewer bar on the ground floor of GROOVE Shinsaibashi East, open from 16:00 to midnight, with an 8-seat counter that suits solo drinkers since skewers can be ordered one at a time. Alongside juicy yakitori it grills pork skewers and a spicy offal, and the soft-cartilage kara-age and doteyaki are worth ordering; one diner loved the sweet potato with honey mayo. Seasoning runs strong and rich, made for drinking, with ¥500 draft beer and highballs poured to the brim. A chopstick lottery comes with handwritten notes. Service opinions split: two diners found staff cheerful, two found them curt or pushy.

anecdotes.text: "The yakitori is grilled carefully, one skewer at a time, which is truly appreciated by solo diners… the best accompaniment is the kara-age of soft cartilage and the flavorful doteyaki." — April 2026.
"I was very pleased to find that draft beer was JPY 500, tax included… All the staff were energetic and cheerful…" — May 2026.

osaka_shu_shu_sake_bar_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Sake bar · a wood-toned sake bar with creative small plates, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A stylish fourth-floor sake bar in GROOVE Shinsaibashi East, warm wood inside, with a sake list that changes each visit, plus gin, shochu and whisky. The food is more than snacks: taro dumplings with beef and burdock in a nameko sauce, spring cabbage and prosciutto croquettes, Kagoshima chicken sashimi, fatty bluefin and seared mackerel, and in spring a run of firefly-squid dishes ending in clay-pot rice. The deep-fried house curry bread is a good take-home. Book a course for better value than ordering à la carte. Pretty sake cups and tableware. Rules: one non-alcoholic drinker per group, two-hour limit when busy. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Sake bar with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

"…I took home a homemade curry bread as a souvenir. Apparently, [the shop takes] bread, fill[s] it with curry, and deep-fr[ies] it…" — July 2026.

osaka_kogaryu_honten_amerikamura.notes: [Takoyaki · Amerikamura's 1974 takoyaki stand by Triangle Park] The original shop of Koga Ryu, a takoyaki stand across from Amerikamura's Triangle Park since 1974, now with about nine shops. Ten small balls come per serving, soft and gooey rather than crisp, with a strong dashi flavor and big pieces of octopus. One diner calls the classic sauce-and-mayo (¥600) the most popular; another was told that Koga Ryu was the first to put mayonnaise on takoyaki. The negi versions come buried under green onion, with sauce (¥700) or ponzu. Eat upstairs or take them to the park. Two diners say Osaka locals pointed them here instead of Dotonbori. PayPay or cash only.

chef_bio.origin: Founded 1974 (Tabelog); the main shop of about nine (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The most popular dish, the sauce mayo takoyaki, features a fluffy and gooey batter infused with dashi! The special mayonnaise is rich yet not overwhelming…" — October 2026.
"I ordered the negi sauce version for JPY 700, tax included… the takoyaki is so generously garnished with green onions that you can hardly see the balls themselves." — October 2026.

osaka_naniwa_soba_namba_dining_maison.notes: [Soba · soba-shabu and meat dipping soba on Takashimaya's restaurant floor, Namba] The Takashimaya branch of Naniwa Soba, a small Osaka soba chain (four shops) on the seventh-floor restaurant level, with colorful seats. The signature, trademarked, is soba-shabu: Wagyu swished through the house dashi and eaten with fresh soba, as a course from ¥5,000. For a simpler meal, one repeat visitor always picks the meat dipping soba (¥1,300), pork in a lightly spicy chili-oil dip that becomes a rich soup when you add soba water at the end. Also chilled sudachi soba, ume-and-yam soba and an oyakodon set; diners praise the delicate Kansai-style broth. Open to 21:30 or 22:00, later than many department-store restaurants.

chef_bio.origin: Branch of Naniwa Soba, a local chain of four (September 2026 review); opened 2 March 2010 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: Soba restaurant in Takashimaya Osaka, with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "…the spicy oil-flavored Niku Tsuke (JPY 1300). It was packed with plenty of pork and soba… When I added the leftover dipping sauce to the soba-yu (soba water) at the end, it transformed into a rich pork-based soup." — September 2026.
"Each dish was generous in portion, and the broth had a delicate, light flavor that was refined in the Kansai style." — September 2026.

osaka_ola_tacos_bar_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Mexican · a late-night taco and tequila bar since 2001, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small Mexican bar near Shinsaibashi, open since 2001 and late into the night, with a neon 'Tacos' sign, a terrace and a Latin, clink-glasses mood. Tacos come on handmade tortillas: chorizo with tangy salsa, tender braised pork rib (¥880), pulled pork with beans, or cheese-filled. Start with the shrimp-and-avocado cocktail de camarón (¥1,320) and a crisp garlic-mushroom quesadilla. About 30 salsas sit ready for heat-seekers, and the tequila and mezcal list is deep; one diner who doesn't care for tequila found the tequila soda easy to drink. One diner found the chicken taco's mayo-like sauce unexpected. Book ahead: food can run out late. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Mexican taco and tequila bar (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Mexican food is about chili aroma and flavor more than heat (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Tacos on handmade tortillas; tequila and mezcal.

anecdotes.text: "Cocktail de Camaron (JPY 1,320, tax included) — Shrimp and avocado marinated with tomato and lime… Tacos de Costilla (JPY 880, tax included) — Tacos made with tender braised pork rib." — June 2026.
"The tacos were authentically delicious, featuring pulled pork and a bean paste, and the tortillas were especially tasty." — September 2026.

osaka_j_bowl_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Tabelog lists Monday 19:00–23:00 and Tue–Sun and holidays 19:00–04:00, with irregular closures, yet reviews describe lunch visits and the listing says seating changes between lunch and dinner, so check before going. One diner arrived at 22:45 for a booking to find it closing and was given takeout (August 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Designated smoking area (Tabelog). Children and pets welcome; takeout and delivery (Tabelog).
osaka_j_bowl_shinsaibashi.notes: [Café · thick açaí bowls and Greek yogurt in a bar-like room, Shinsaibashi] A small açaí-bowl and Greek-yogurt shop near Shinsaibashi Station with a dim, bar-like room and plush sofas. The açaí is thick and creamy, piled with fruit and honey, and you can build your own with granola, kiwi, coconut, nuts or mango; the Greek yogurt with comb honey is rich and filling. Bowls run about ¥1,680, which diners call a little pricey. Two diners called it the best açaí bowl ever, but one found a smaller, unripe-mango bowl on a return visit. Tabelog lists vegan options. Hours are unclear (the listing shows evenings to 4 am, reviewers came at lunch), so check before you go.

chef_bio.specialty: Açaí bowls; Greek yogurt with comb honey.

anecdotes.text: "…the acai was thick and creamy, loaded with fruits, and generously drizzled with honey! The interior had a bar-like atmosphere… we could relax comfortably on the plush sofas." — June 2026, about ¥1,680.
"I ordered the Greek yogurt with comb honey. The yogurt was quite rich and filling." — April 2026.

osaka_roco_pizza_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 17:30–24:00 (last order 23:30); may change, so check (Tabelog). One-drink rule (June 2025). Cards accepted (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Backless wooden stools at small tables (2018).
osaka_roco_pizza_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Pizza · a cheap oven-baked pizza bar, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small Italian-bar-style pizza place in the Higashi-Shinsaibashi drinking streets, known for cheap, chewy, rustic pizzas that are on the small side, so a group can order several. Diners like the Margherita, a basil pizza, the quattro formaggi with honey and a mentaiko pizza, with ahijo and prosciutto to start and inexpensive wine. There's a one-drink rule. Pizzas were ¥500–600 in older reviews; recent prices aren't reported. Service reports range from attentive (pizzas sent one at a time so each stays hot) to curt, and one diner found the backless stools hard going after an hour. Most reviews are older; the latest is June 2025.

anecdotes.text: "The size of the pizza is a bit smaller, but it's just the right size and has a rustic homemade flavor. There is a one-drink policy. My favorite is the Quattro Formaggi with honey." — June 2025.
"The pizzas were about JPY 600 each, and we enjoyed authentic, oven-baked varieties. They were fluffy and delicious." — February 2020.

osaka_sushi_keyaki_shinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · a quiet 8-seat Edomae counter near Amerikamura, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, upstairs Edomae sushi counter of eight seats on the quieter edge of Amerikamura, open since 2014 and serving lunch as well as dinner. Each piece arrives already seasoned, with salt, citrus or plum paste instead of soy sauce. The ¥20,000 omakase runs like a small kaiseki: appetizer, three sashimi, grilled fish and chawanmushi before ten nigiri from squid and striped jack to chutoro, sea urchin and eel; there's also a ¥12,000 sushi course and lunch courses that diners call good value. Past highlights include tuna cooked in a salt crust, well-judged kohada and bonito with salt. You can ask for less rice. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Counter sushi restaurant with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2020–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fish sourced each morning, seasoned piece by piece (Tabelog listing; April 2026).

anecdotes.text: "'Sushi without Soy Sauce' seasoned for each topping — Delicate flavors enhanced with salt, citrus, and plum paste." — April 2026, Omakase Course ¥20,000.
"That day, we enjoyed tuna done in a salt crust, which was rich in flavor. The kohada (gizzard shad) was perfectly seasoned with vinegar…" — March 2023.

osaka_teppan_dining_yo_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a calm wooden teppan bar off Amerikamura, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A tidy, wood-lined teppan bar tucked away in Nishi-Shinsaibashi, a quiet alternative to the Dotonbori okonomiyaki queues. Okonomiyaki comes in several styles, pork, oyster, a mixed modern and even Hiroshima-style, served on individual pans; around it, yam-yaki, cheese tonpei-yaki, shrimp mayo, shrimp toast and a salty, well-liked soba-meshi, plus salt-grilled offal and thick beef tongue. One diner didn't care for the sauce. One person runs the kitchen, so it can be slow, but diners like the warm touches (a message card on the table, a candy on the way out) and fair prices. Tabelog lists vegan options; ask.

chef_bio.background: Teppan and okonomiyaki bar run by its owner, who cooks alone (September 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I tried shrimp toast for the first time, which was like toast topped with shrimp chili, and it was delightful! The cheese tonpei-yaki was, as expected, delicious and paired perfectly with beer!" — September 2026.
"I had the mixed modern okonomiyaki as my main dish. Instead of being served on a teppan table, it came out on an individual frying pan-like plate." — May 2024.
